content.text: The count is up to 327 and three toys are working on the fourth sleeper. The wake costs keep rising, so I'll stop here at about 3 minutes.

I played for about 3 minutes and 13 seconds, then ended the session.

**What I think the game is:** a calm incremental (clicker/idle) game set in a dark tailor's or toymaker's workshop at night. You wind a big brass key on a gear to earn spirals. A thread links the gear to one sleeping wind-up toy, and a ring on that toy's key fills as spirals build up. When the ring is full, the spirals are spent automatically and the toy wakes up. Each awake toy earns spirals on its own, walks over with the others to help wind the next sleeper, and adds a small gear to the main machine. Parts of the room also come back to life: a table lamp lit up, and a red sewing machine was uncovered and started running.

**Progress:** I woke 3 of about 15 toys, and the machine grew three small gears. The wake cost rose each time (roughly 40, then about 120, then around 200+), but passive income grew fast enough that the last fill only took about 20 seconds.

**What I understood:**
- Clicking or holding the gear gives one spiral per wind, and holding winds continuously.
- Waking happens automatically when a toy's ring fills.
- Awake toys produce spirals passively.

**What confused me:**
- A tutorial hand on the gear's hub made me think holding there was needed to wake a toy. The second hold only kept winding, so the wake just happens when the ring fills.
- There's no shop or upgrade menu, so I'm not sure whether the player makes any choices or only winds.
- I never found a use for the glowing face orb near the shelf, and clicking a toy did nothing.
- The grandfather clock's hands moved, so it might track some kind of night or time limit.
- I didn't try the button in the top-left corner (a sparkle icon) or the round arrow at top right, which looks like a restart.

**Would I keep playing?** For a while, yes. It looks good, and seeing the room warm up and the toys gather to wind each other is satisfying. I'd want to know what the clock and the orb do and whether the rest of the workshop (the dress form, the clock) wakes up too. But if winding is the only real action, it could get repetitive once the novelty wears off.
